sec: AIH presentation tree, LFT/fibroscan, laboratory markers and antibody tables

items.q: The presentation tree of AIH has three arms. Which is NOT one of them?
items.exp: Arms: Acute Hepatitis; Chronic hepatitis; Cirrhosis with complications. Cholestasis is explicitly 'Not seen in AIH' (bottom note). (Book p1024)

items.q: Acute-hepatitis arm — judge: I Presents with waxing and waning of jaundice. II Presents as non-resolving acute hepatitis.
items.exp: 'Waxing & waning of jaundice' and 'Non-resolving acute hepatitis' are the two printed bullets. (Book p1024)

items.q: In the acute-hepatitis arm, what does the book instruct as the '1st rule out'?
items.exp: '1st Rule out → HAV, HBV, HEV'. (Book p1024)

items.q: If HAV, HBV and HEV are all negative in that arm, which three entities does the flowchart then say to rule out / consider?
opts: Wilson's disease, autoimmune disease (ANA +ve), fulminant hepatic failure (rare)
Primary biliary cirrhosis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, IgG4 disease
CMV, EBV and HCV post-transfusion hepatitis (rare)
items.exp: 'If all are negative then rule out → Wilson's ds / Autoimmune disease (ANA +ve) / Fulminant hepatic failure (rare)'. (Book p1024)

items.q: Chronic-hepatitis arm: which symptom–sign pair is highlighted first?
items.exp: 'Fatigue & Hepatomegaly' + 'With autoimmune background: Rheumatoid arthritis, SLE'. (Book p1024)

items.q: Fill up: In the chronic arm the arrow toward cirrhosis is annotated 'Jaundice + Splenomegaly — ______/______ progression'.
items.exp: The connecting arrow reads 'Jaundice + Splenomegaly — Rare/slow progression' toward cirrhosis with complications. (Book p1024)

items.q: 'Then do LFT' in the chronic arm yields what typical enzyme pattern?
opts: ↑ ALT and AST (<150 U/L), ALT > AST
↑ ALT and AST (>1000 U/L), AST > ALT
items.exp: '↑ ALT and AST (<150 U/ltr), ALT > AST' → then Fibroscan. (Book p1024)

items.q: After LFT in the chronic-hepatitis arm, what is the next arrow in the flowchart?
Cirrhosis-with-complications arm lists three complications. Which is NOT printed?
items.exp: 'Portal HTN; Liver failure; Hepatocellular carcinoma: (Significant risk) – Also in Hemochromatosis.' (Book p1024)

items.q: Fill up: Under HCC in the AIH cirrhosis arm the book notes the significant risk is 'Also in ______'.
items.exp: 'Hepatocellular carcinoma : (Significant risk) – Also in Hemochromatosis.' (Book p1024)

items.q: Laboratory markers: A/G ratio reversal with ↑ globulin leads to which confirmatory test and finding?
opts: Serum free light chain assay / immunofixation: monoclonal M-band
Complement C3 / C4 assay: consumption with low levels
Bone marrow aspirate / trephine: reactive plasmacytosis
items.exp: 'A/G ratio reversal : ↑ Globulin → Immunoelectrophoresis / Protein electrophoresis : Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia'. (Book p1024)

items.q: Type-I AIH antibody table — match — 1) ANA 2) Anti actin antibody (AAA) 3) Anti SLA … A) Most specific, poor prognosis B) 100% +ve C) Poor prognosis
items.exp: ANA = 100% +ve; Anti SMA (no feature printed); AAA = Poor prognosis; Anti SLA (soluble liver antigen) = most specific, poor prognosis. (Book p1024)

items.q: Fill up: 'Anti SLA' in the Type-I table stands for anti ______ antigen.
items.exp: 'Anti SLA (Soluble liver antigen) — most specific, poor prognosis'. (Book p1024)

items.q: Atypical p-ANCA in the Type-I table is 'seen in' three conditions. Which is NOT one of them?
items.exp: 'Seen in : AIH, Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, Ulcerative colitis.' PBC is the AMA condition in the note below. (Book p1024)

items.q: Type-II AIH table — match — 1) Anti LKM-1 2) Anti liver cytosol type-1 … A) Poor prognosis B) Also seen in HCV infection
items.exp: Anti LKM-1 : Also seen HCV infection; Anti liver cytosol type-1 : Poor prognosis. (Book p1024)

items.q: Note beside the Type-II table — match — 1) Anti LKM-2 2) Anti LKM-3 … A) HDV infection B) Drug induced hepatitis
items.exp: 'Anti LKM-2 : Drug induced hepatitis; Anti LKM-3 : HDV infection'. (Book p1024)

items.q: A young woman with suspected AIH has pruritus, hyperpigmentation and weight loss, and her serum is AMA-positive. Per the bottom Note on this page, how should this be read?
opts: Cholestasis with AMA points to primary biliary cirrhosis — this triad is not seen in AIH
Classic Type-I AIH with cholestatic onset — start steroid 1 mg/kg/day
Type-II AIH with hyperpigmentation — confirm with anti-LKM-1 and liver cytosol-1
AIH–PSC overlap with cholestatic features — order MRCP for strictures
items.exp: Note: 'Antimitochondrial Antibody : Primary biliary cirrhosis. Cholestasis : Pruritis + hyperpigmentation + weightloss (Not seen in AIH)'. (Book p1024)
